clue.text: Fool bathes with bloodsucker

parts.note: bathes as in takes a quick dip, so dips
a tick is a parasite that feeds on blood

explanation.surface: A bather finds a leech or tick attached, and feels a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal insult: a stupid person is called a dipstick in casual slang.

clue.text: I have to follow terrible court order

indicators.note: these words come after the rest

parts.note: dire means dreadful or terrible
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A judge's order described as terrible by someone obliged to obey it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' places I've at the end; CT is the usual short form of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official instruction, an order or command.

clue.text: Standard necklace has centrepiece of granite rather than diamonds

indicators.note: one letter is used in place of the other

parts.note: a pendant is a necklace with a hanging ornament
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

indicators.note: the central letter of granite

explanation.surface: A jeweller's necklace with a granite stone instead of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather than' swaps the D of PENDANT for N, the middle of granite.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a standard is a flag, and a long tapering flag on a ship is a pennant.

clue.text: Time wasted by son; little changes

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter sits next to the rest

parts.note: wasted away, so weak

explanation.surface: A son wasting time and making only small adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: minor adjustments or fine-tunings made to something.

clue.text: Largely informal seminars

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: colloquial means informal in speech

explanation.surface: Seminars described as mostly casual affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' takes the last L from COLLOQUIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of colloquium: an academic conference or seminar.

clue.text: Suddenly burst into appreciative noise when taken from behind during sex

indicators.note: during places the reversed noise inside the word for sex

parts.note: IT is a coy old euphemism for sex

indicators.note: read from the back, so the noise word is written backwards

parts.note: a contented cat makes a purr

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a noise of pleasure suddenly bursting out mid-act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from behind' reverses the purr; 'during' sets it inside IT, a coy old word for sex appeal or sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to irrupt is to enter forcibly or suddenly, as a crowd bursting into a room.

clue.text: Can cycling muck up acting?

indicators.note: the first letter moves round to the end

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: mire is muddy muck

explanation.surface: Asking whether riding a bicycle could spoil a stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' turns TIN into INT; 'up' reverses MIRE to ERIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an acting head serves in a temporary, provisional capacity.

clue.text: Perhaps Arab people start to regret wearing stockings

parts.note: a race is a people

indicators.note: wearing means the letter is clothed by the stockings

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings

indicators.note: the first letter of regret

explanation.surface: A people who begin to regret wearing stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts R inside HOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Arabian is a famous breed of racing horse, so an Arab may be one.

clue.text: Friends with webbed feet

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Friends who happen to have webbed feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friends' is plural because it supplies two friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoology term: having toes joined by a web, as in the feet of ducks.

clue.text: Inebriated naked dash

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters are taken off

parts.note: inebriated means drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk streaker making a dash across the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips D and K from the outside of DRUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dash is a quick sprint, the same as a short run.

clue.text: Cryptic clue originally "It'll leap about across India"

indicators.note: across means the jumbled letters stretch over the other pair
about signals that these letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: originally means the start of the word clue is used

explanation.surface: A setter describing a cryptic clue about a leaping creature that crosses India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IT'LL LEAP into ELLIPTAL; 'across' puts it round I plus C, after ELLIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: elliptical speech is terse and obscure, leaving meaning to be inferred, as cryptic speech does.

clue.text: Drugs making one crazy

parts.note: crack is a smokable form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A warning that taking drugs will make someone go mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drugs' is plural because it supplies two drugs, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: crackpot ideas are eccentric and wildly unsound, i.e. mad.

clue.text: Cook leftover food, ultimately, for what? To consume

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of for

parts.note: eh? is a casual way of saying what?
to consume food is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone baffled at the point of cooking leftovers if nobody will eat them.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: warming up already-cooked food from an earlier meal is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: A bit constrained by Riot Act

indicators.note: held inside the words Riot Act, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: Someone a little restrained after being read the Riot Act.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the Greek letter's name is used for a tiny amount, as in not one jot.

clue.text: Previously mentioned ideas for a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Ideas for writing a novel that someone already brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a legal word for things already referred to earlier.

clue.text: When optimists buy ammunition to take aim

indicators.note: the first word takes in, or holds, the second

parts.note: a bullet is a round of ammunition
a mark is a target to aim at

explanation.surface: Buying bullets in order to shoot at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' means the ammunition word swallows the aim word. The definition is a whole phrase describing a period of rising share prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance term: a rising stock market, when confident investors buy shares expecting gains.

clue.text: Lacking energy, teach girl to dance

indicators.note: dance makes the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Teaching a girl to dance when lacking energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sluggish and listless, with no get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Stroll around in river? I don't believe it

indicators.note: in means placed inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: around means these letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to have walked around in a river, met with disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges STROLL to LLSTOR; 'in' sets it inside the Tay, the longest river in Scotland. The definition is a spoken reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an exaggerated, unlikely tale that prompts the incredulous retort.

clue.text: Some splats can result if solution is drunk

definitions.text: Some splats can result if solution is drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering about into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning about the messy consequences of drinking a certain laxative solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges SOME SPLATS; read whole, the clue describes the purgative effect of drinking the stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium sulphate dissolved in water is taken as a laxative, hence the messy consequences.

clue.text: Tradesman's ideal job finally about to turn up

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for is, so the definition reads as Tradesman is

parts.note: a plum job is the ideal one, so plum means ideal

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means writing the letters bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of job

explanation.surface: A tradesman's dream: an ideal job finally coming along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses RE plus B (the last of job); in a down answer, up means read upwards. The 's is short for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who fits pipes and fixes leaks is a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Male in bed with queen, getting kiss

indicators.note: in places the male inside the bed

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A royal scandal: a man in bed with the queen, receiving a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a smacker is a loud, hearty kiss, often called a smacker on the lips.

clue.text: Returning after the expected time with other people

indicators.note: coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: arriving after the expected time is being late

explanation.surface: Someone coming back late, accompanied by companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin abbreviation meaning and others, used after a first named author in citations.

clue.text: From time to time, saucily covered in, say, maple syrup

indicators.note: the alternate letters are wrapped by the tree

parts.note: a maple is an example of a tree

indicators.note: every other letter of saucily is taken

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally and saucily covered in maple syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From time to time' takes ACL from saucily; 'covered in' puts that inside the tree. 'Maple' looks part of the syrup but is an example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thick sweet syrup from refining sugar, the British name for molasses.

clue.text: Prisoner and scoundrel agree

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A prisoner and a rogue reaching agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be of the same opinion, to go along with.

clue.text: I'm frightened to go round ancient city area, providing I've found it

indicators.note: the cry is made to surround the city

parts.note: eek! is a cry of fright
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A nervous traveller touring an ancient site, with a hint of discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' has the cry of fright surround Ur, the Mesopotamian city crosswords love; 'providing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation: Archimedes' Greek exclamation literally means I have discovered it.

clue.text: Member of the aristocracy jokes in pubs

indicators.note: in places the jokes inside the pubs

parts.note: bars are drinking establishments
ones, as in have you heard the one about...

explanation.surface: A posh lady telling jokes down the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the jokes inside the pubs; jokes are ones as in 'have you heard the one about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank: a woman holding the lowest rank of the British peerage, or a baron's wife.

clue.text: Beginning to believe what my poorer crosswords do reveals bad spelling?

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of believe

parts.note: the setter jokes that his weaker puzzles lack magic

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating setter admitting that some puzzles fall flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad spelling' means evil spells, not poor orthography.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: malign sorcery is literally wicked spell-casting, i.e. witchcraft used for harm.

clue.text: Bird doesn't finish making bird sound

indicators.note: the final letter is not completed, so it drops off

parts.note: a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A bird stopping short of finishing its call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't finish' cuts the last letter off COOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the soft murmuring call of a pigeon or dove.

clue.text: One who deals in Communist paintings, perhaps, in revolution

indicators.note: revolving round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: red is a common term for a Communist
paintings are one example of art

explanation.surface: A Communist art dealer caught up in a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' reverses REDART.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dealer is a merchant who buys and sells goods.

clue.text: Under no circumstances worry lady on vacation about onset of cholera

indicators.note: about means the other letters go round this one

parts.note: to scare is to frighten or worry

indicators.note: onset means the first letter of cholera
vacated, so only the outer letters of lady remain

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a woman away on holiday should not fret about catching cholera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside SCARELY, after SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: as in scarcely ever, the adverb means hardly, almost not at all.
